en: The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Attainment of Great Buddhahood, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of Kucha during the Yao Qin dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Mount Pāṣa in the kingdom of Magadha.

Gujue (Solitary and Remote) Mountain—where the Buddhas of the past constantly descended to subdue Māra—during the summer retreat, [the Buddha] walked up and down on the mountain peak with Śāriputra and spoke this verse:
“Listen with single-minded attention!
The Great Samādhi of Radiant Light, a person of incomparable merit, is about to appear in the world.
That person shall preach the sublime Dharma, so that all may attain full satisfaction;
like a thirsty person drinking nectar, they will swiftly reach the path of liberation.

At that time, the fourfold assembly leveled the roads, sprinkled water, swept clean, and burned incense; they all gathered together, bringing various offerings to honor the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus.
They gazed intently upon the Tathāgata, like a filial son beholding his compassionate father;
their longing for the Dharma-father was like that of one parched with thirst yearning for a drink.

With one mind, they desired to entreat the Dharma King to turn the wheel of the true Dharma; their faculties remained unmoving, their thoughts succeeding one another in a continuous stream directed toward the Buddha.

At that time, the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans each rose from their seats, circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right, prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, and wept tears toward the Buddha.

At that time, the Greatly Wise Śāriputra adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder, and—knowing the mind of the Dharma King, being well able to accord with it, and having studied under the Buddha-Dharma King to turn the wheel of the sublime Dharma—he, as a minister to the Buddha and a great general upholding the Dharma, out of compassion for sentient beings and desiring to cause them to be liberated from the bonds of suffering, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"Previously, on the mountain peak, the Tathāgata spoke verses in praise of the foremost wise ones—teachings never before set forth in the sūtras of past or present.

All in this great assembly now yearn with hearts like parched land, their tears falling like heavy rain, desiring to hear the Tathāgata speak of future buddhas and open the path to the nectar of immortality."
By what roots of goodness, by what precepts, and by what acts of giving do you attain Maitreya’s name, his merits, his spiritual powers, and the adornments of his land?
What is concentration?
What is wisdom?
By what power of knowledge can one behold Maitreya?
"In what state of mind does one cultivate the Eightfold Noble Path?

When Śāriputra asked this question, hundreds of thousands of devaputras and countless Brahmā kings joined their palms in reverent salutation and, with one voice, together posed this question, addressing the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!"
May we, in future ages, behold Maitreya—the greatest fruition among men, the eye and light of the triple world—who universally preaches great compassion for all sentient beings.
The eight classes of beings likewise all joined their palms in reverence and entreated the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Brahmā King and his host of Brahmās, with one voice and in unison, joined their palms in praise and spoke these verses:
“Homage to the Full Moon, who is endowed with the ten powers!”
A general of great diligence, courageous and fearless;
an omniscient one who has transcended the three realms of existence;
having perfected the three types of supernormal knowledge, he has subdued the four māras.
Being a vessel of the Dharma, the mind is like space;
tranquil and unmoving, it neither exists nor does not exist,
neither is non-existent nor is it not non-existent, thus attaining realization of the dharma of emptiness.
"Praised by the world, we, with one mind, take refuge all at once; we pray that you turn the wheel of Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One said to Śāriputra:
"I shall explain this to you in detail and with full analysis. Listen attentively, listen attentively!"
Reflect upon this well!
You who now, with a most excellent and virtuous mind,

wish to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding the unsurpassed path of practice and the Mahāprajñāpāramitā— the Tathāgata perceives this clearly, as if looking at an āmalaka fruit in the palm of his hand.
He addressed Śāriputra:
"If, in the presence of the seven Buddhas of the past, one hears their names, pays homage, and makes offerings, by these causes and conditions, one shall purify and eliminate karmic obstructions."

Furthermore, having heard the root of Maitreya’s great compassion, you have attained a pure mind; you should now with single-mindedness join your palms and take refuge in the Great Compassionate One of the future, and I shall explain it to you in detail and with full analysis.

In the land of Maitreya Buddha, one proceeds from pure livelihood; there is no flattery or hypocrisy. One attains the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of wisdom, yet remains without receiving or attachment.

By means of the great adornment of the ten subtle vows, they cause all sentient beings to give rise to a supple mind; they come to be embraced by the great compassion of Maitreya, are born in that land, subdue their faculties, and accord with the Buddha’s transformation.

“Śāriputra! The surface of the waters of the four great oceans shall each decrease by three thousand yojanas. At that time, the land of Jambudvīpa will be exactly ten thousand yojanas in length and breadth, and its ground will be level, pure, and clear like a mirror of lapis lazuli.”

There were flowers of great delight, flowers that gladden the mind, flowers of supreme fragrance, *utpala* flowers, flowers with large golden petals, flowers with petals of the seven treasures, and flowers with petals of white silver; their filaments were soft and supple like celestial silks.
They produced auspicious fruits, perfect in both fragrance and flavor, as soft as celestial cotton.

The groves of trees were in full bloom with exquisite, sweet fruits, growing so luxuriantly that they surpassed even Śakra’s Nandana Garden; these trees were lofty and prominent, reaching a height of thirty li.

The cities and towns are situated so close together that a rooster can fly from one to the next; all have planted great roots of goodness under the present Buddha and, as a reward for their practice of a compassionate mind, have been born together in that land.

Their wisdom and majestic virtue, their five sensory pleasures and various requisites, and their happiness and security are such that they suffer neither from cold, heat, wind, nor fire, nor do they experience the nine kinds of afflictions. Their lifespan is full, reaching eighty-four thousand years, and none die prematurely. Every human body is sixteen *zhang* tall, and they daily enjoy the most exquisite peace and bliss, taking delight in dwelling within deep meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
There are only three ailments:
first, hunger and thirst; second, the need for excretion; and third, old age;
women do not marry until they are five hundred years old.

“There is a great city named Kukkutapāda, twelve hundred yojanas in length and breadth and seven yojanas in height, adorned with the seven treasures. Seven-jeweled pavilions are spontaneously manifested there, exquisite and wondrous in their dignity, beautifully ornamented and pure.”
Between the windows and casements were arrayed various precious women, each holding in her hand a net of pearls, adorned with various jewels to cover them above;
precious bells were suspended closely together, their sounds like celestial music.

There were rows of trees made of the seven treasures, interspersed with canals and springs, all formed of the seven treasures, flowing with waters of different colors that reflected one another; they flowed crosswise and slowly, without obstructing one another. On both banks, pure golden sand was spread. The streets, lanes, and pathways were twelve li wide and entirely pure, like a celestial garden, swept clean and pristine.
“There is a great dragon king named Tālaśikhin, fully endowed with merit and majestic power.

His pond is near the city, and his palace, like a tower of the seven treasures, is visible from without. Constantly at midnight, he transforms himself into the likeness of a man and, using an auspicious vase filled with fragrant, colored water, sprinkles it over the dust and soil. The ground becomes moist and lustrous, as if smeared with oil; thus, as people pass to and fro, there is no dust or grime.”

"At that time, due to the merit of the people of the world, there were pillars of great pearls at every intersection and thoroughfare. Their radiance was like that of the sun, illuminating eighty *yojanas* in each of the four directions; they were of pure golden hue, and their brilliant glow made no difference between day and night, such that the light of oil lamps and candles appeared like a mass of ink."

Fragrant breezes blew at intervals, blowing upon the pillars of bright pearls and raining down precious necklaces for all the people to use; those who wore them experienced a natural bliss like that of the third dhyāna.

Everywhere there were gold, silver, rare treasures, and maṇi jewels, accumulated in heaps as high as mountains. These jewel mountains emitted light that shone universally throughout the city; all the people who encountered it were filled with joy and gave rise to the bodhicitta.
"There is a great yakṣa deity named Bhadrapāla-saikya—whose name in the language of Qin means 'Good Instruction'—who day and night protects the city of Ketumatī and its inhabitants."

The ground was swept clean; should anyone need to relieve themselves, the earth would crack open to receive them, and once they had finished, it would close back up, producing red lotuses to conceal any foul odor.

At that time, when the people of the world grew old and decrepit, they would naturally go to the mountains and forests beneath the trees to dwell in peaceful seclusion. Mindful of the Buddha until the end of their lives, most were reborn in the Great Brahma Heaven or before the presence of various Buddhas upon their death.

“That land is peaceful and secure, free from the calamities of enemies, bandits, or robbers; in its cities and villages, no one keeps their gates closed, nor does it suffer the hardships of decline, affliction, water, fire, weapons, or the toxic perils of famine.

People there are always compassionate in heart, respectful and harmonious, with their sense faculties subdued; they love one another as a son loves his father or a mother loves her child, and their speech is humble and modest. All this is due to the guidance of Maitreya’s compassionate mind and because they uphold the precept against killing and refrain from eating meat. By these causes and conditions, those born in that land have tranquil sense faculties, upright countenances, and are endowed with majestic marks, like celestial youths.
Furthermore, there were eighty-four thousand small cities made of various jewels as its retinue, with the city of Ketumatī situated at its center.
Whether men and women, great or small, were far or near, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, they were all able to see one another without any obstruction.

Luminous maṇi wish-fulfilling jewel flowers filled the world, raining down bowls of seven-jeweled flowers, *tāma* flowers, *utpala* flowers, *kumuda* flowers, *puṇḍarīka* flowers, *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, and *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers, which spread across the ground;
or else, driven by the wind, they circled in the air.

At that time, within the boundaries of that land—its cities, towns, and villages, its gardens, groves, bathing pools, springs, rivers, and marshes—there naturally existed water endowed with the eight meritorious qualities.

Jīvajīvaka birds, geese, ducks, ruddy sheldrakes, peacocks, parrots, *śuka* birds, *mayūra* birds, *śāri* birds, sweet-voiced birds, pigeons, eagles, *rāji-paśava* birds, *pratyakṣadarśin* birds, and others produced wondrous sounds.
Furthermore, there were countless other species of birds with exquisite voices, gathering and sporting in the forests and ponds.

There were golden, stainless, pure radiance flowers; sorrowless, pure wisdom-sun radiance flowers; fresh white seven-day fragrance flowers; and *campaka* six-colored fragrance flowers. There were hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of flowers born of water and land—blue with blue light, yellow with yellow light, red with red light, and white with white light. Their fragrance was incomparably pure, blooming constantly day and night, never withering.
There were wish-fulfilling fruit trees, incomparably fragrant and beautiful, filling the realm.
Fragrant trees with golden light grew amidst jewel mountains, filling the realm and emitting pleasing scents that universally perfumed everything.
"At that time, Jambudvīpa will always possess excellent fragrances, like a mountain of incense.
Its flowing waters will be beautiful, their taste sweet and capable of removing afflictions, and rain will fall according to the seasons."

In the celestial gardens, fragrant and exquisite varieties of rice ripen; by the power of the devas, a single sowing yields seven harvests with very little labor and a vast yield. The grain grows luxuriantly, free from weeds and impurities.

Through the karmic fruit of the past merits of sentient beings, when food enters their mouths, it is digested and transformed; it possesses a hundred flavors, its fragrance and beauty are peerless, and it fills them with physical strength.
At that time, there was a Wheel-Turning Sage King in that land named Śaṅkha.

He possessed fourfold armies, yet he governed the four continents not by military force but through majestic virtue; he was endowed with the thirty-two marks and secondary characteristics of a Great Man.
The king had a thousand sons, all valiant and handsome, who naturally subdued his enemies.
The king possessed seven treasures:
first, the precious golden wheel, with its thousand spokes, hub, and rim all fully complete;
second, the precious white elephant, as white as the Snow Mountains, with its seven limbs planted firmly upon the ground, majestic and magnificent to behold like the King of Mountains.
Third, the horse-treasure is dark blue, with vermilion manes and tails; beneath its hooves flowers bloom, and its hooves and hoofs are made of the seven treasures.
Fourth, the jewel-treasure is brilliant and clearly visible, two cubits in length; it rains down jewels from its radiance, fulfilling the wishes of sentient beings.
Fifth, the Woman-Jewel (strī-ratna), whose complexion is exquisite and whose body is supple and boneless.
Sixth, the Treasurer-Minister (gṛhapati-ratna), from whose mouth jewels issue forth, from beneath whose feet a rain of jewels falls, and from whose two hands jewels emerge.
Seventh, the Minister of Military Affairs: whenever he deems it appropriate to mobilize, the fourfold army emerges from the sky like a mass of clouds.
His thousand sons, the seven treasures, and all the people within his realm look upon one another without harboring ill will, loving each other as a mother loves her child.

At that time, the king’s thousand sons each took precious jewels and constructed a terrace of the seven treasures before the main hall; it was thirty stories high and thirteen yojanas in length, featuring a thousand heads and a thousand wheels, moving with sovereign ease.
There are four great treasuries, each of which is surrounded by four hundred million smaller treasuries.
The great treasury of Iṣvāka is located in the kingdom of Gandhāra;
the great treasury of Pañcāla is located in the kingdom of Mithilā.
The great treasury of Piṅgala is in the kingdom of Surāṣṭra;
the great treasury of Rāghava is in the kingdom of Vārāṇasī, at the site of the Mountain of the Ancient Sages.

These four great treasuries spontaneously open up, manifesting a great radiance; they are one thousand yojanas in length and breadth, filled with precious jewels, each accompanied by four hundred million smaller treasuries, and each is guarded by four great nāgas.
These four great treasuries and various minor treasuries spontaneously emerged, their forms like lotus flowers.

Countless people all went together to behold them; at that time, although the many jewels had no guardians, when the multitude saw them, their hearts felt no greed or attachment, and they cast them upon the ground as if they were tiles, stones, grass, wood, or clods of earth.
Those of that time who saw it felt a sense of weary detachment and said to one another:

"As the Buddha has taught, in the past sentient beings, for the sake of this treasure, mutually harmed one another, stole from one another, practiced deception, and spoke falsehoods; thus they caused the conditions for the suffering of birth and death to increase ever further, falling into the great hells."

In the city of Ketumatī, nets of various jewels cover it from above; adorned with precious bells, when stirred by a gentle breeze, their sound is harmonious and elegant, like the striking of bells and chimes, proclaiming refuge in the Buddha, refuge in the Dharma, and refuge in the Sangha.
"At that time, there was a great brahmin leader in the city named Śuddhodana, and a brahmin woman named Māyādevī, whose nature was gentle and mild; Maitreya took birth with them as his parents."

Though dwelling within the womb, he was as if wandering through a celestial palace; he emitted great radiance that was unobstructed by dust or defilement. His body was the color of purple gold, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, and he sat upon a precious lotus flower. Sentient beings gazed upon him without ever feeling satiety; his brilliance was so dazzling it could not be fully beheld, never having been seen before by gods or people of the world.
His physical strength was immeasurable; the power of each and every joint surpassed all mighty dragons and elephants.
From his inconceivable pores issued rays of light that shone boundlessly without obstruction.
The sun, moon, constellations, water, fire, and the light of jewels all ceased to appear, becoming like mere dust.

The body of Śākyamuni Buddha was eighty *zhǔ* (cubits) or three hundred and twenty *zhàng* (fathoms) in height; his chest was twenty-five *zhǔ* or one hundred *zhàng* wide; his face was twelve and a half *zhǔ* or fifty *zhàng* long; and his nose was high, straight, and centered upon the mouth. His physical marks were complete, he was peerlessly upright and handsome, and he had perfected the primary and secondary signs of excellence.
Each of his primary marks was adorned with eighty-four thousand secondary signs, like a cast golden image.
From within each secondary sign, light radiated forth, illuminating a thousand yojanas;
his physical eyes were clear and transparent, with the blue and white parts distinct and vivid.
A constant radiance encircles his body, extending for a hundred *yojanas* across his face.

The sun, moon, and stars, as well as pearls, *maṇi* gems, and rows of trees made of the seven treasures, all lose their brilliance in the presence of the Buddha’s light; these other lights no longer serve any purpose. The Buddha’s body is tall and majestic, like a mountain of yellow gold; those who behold it naturally escape the three evil realms.

"At that time, Maitreya clearly contemplated the faults and afflictions of the five worldly desires; he saw that sentient beings were undergoing suffering, submerged in the long-flowing current, and deeply piteous within the great cycle of birth and death!"

With such right mindfulness, he observed suffering, emptiness, and impermanence; he took no pleasure in the household life and grew weary of the confinement of home, regarding it as if it were a prison.

"At that time, King Śaṅkha, together with his ministers, the people of the land, and the populace, took a palanquin made of the seven treasures—equipped with a thousand jeweled canopies, a thousand jeweled eaves, ten billion jeweled bells, ten billion jeweled banners, a thousand jeweled vessels, and a thousand jeweled jars—and presented it to Maitreya."
After Maitreya had accepted them, he gave them to the brahmins;
once the brahmins had received them, they immediately destroyed them and divided them among themselves.
When the brahmins observed that Maitreya was capable of performing such a great act of giving, they conceived a sense of profound wonder and marvel.

Seeing this jeweled terrace vanish in an instant, Maitreya Bodhisattva realized that all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*) are subject to total destruction. Cultivating the perception of impermanence, he recited the verse on the impermanence of the past Buddhas’ cool nectar:
"All conditioned things are impermanent; This is the law of arising and ceasing.
When arising and ceasing have ceased, Cessation is bliss."
Having spoken these verses, he left the household life to study the Path and sat beneath the Dragon-Flower Bodhi tree at the adamantine-adorned site of enlightenment.

Its branches were like precious dragons, emitting flowers of a hundred jewels; each flower and leaf was the color of the seven treasures, and each color bore distinct fruits that accorded with the inclinations of sentient beings. Such things were peerless among gods or humans. The tree was fifty *yojanas* high, its branches and leaves spreading in the four directions and radiating great light.
"At that time, Maitreya, together with eighty-four thousand brahmins, went to the site of enlightenment. Maitreya immediately shaved his hair and left the household life to study the Way;
having gone forth early in the morning, he subdued the four kinds of Māras during the first watch of that very night and attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. He then spoke this verse:
'For a long time I have contemplated the suffering of sentient beings, Desiring to pull them out, yet finding no way to liberate them.'"
Now having realized Bodhi, all is suddenly unobstructed;
I have also penetrated the emptiness of sentient beings, And that their fundamental nature and characteristics are as they truly are.
Henceforth there shall be no more sorrow or suffering, And even compassion is without objective conditions.
Originally, for the sake of saving you all, I gave away my kingdom, city, head, eyes, wife, children, and hands and feet; such acts of giving to others were beyond counting.
Now, at last, I have attained liberation—the unsurpassed, supreme, and great quiescence.
I shall now explain for you, fully opening the path of ambrosia.
Such great fruits and rewards all arise from generosity, ethical discipline, and wisdom;
they are born from the six kinds of great patience, and likewise from great compassion.
"One attains merit free from defilement.
Having spoken this verse, he remained silent.
At that time, the gods, nāgas, and kingly spirits did not manifest their bodies, yet they rained down celestial flowers as an offering to the Buddha.
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways, and light radiated from the Buddha’s body, illuminating immeasurable realms so that all those ready for deliverance were able to behold the Buddha.

At that time, Śakra Devānām-Indra, the World-Protecting Heavenly Kings, Mahābrahmā, and countless sons of gods bowed their heads at his feet in the Flower Forest Garden (*Puṣpavana*), joined their palms, and entreated him to turn the wheel of Dharma.
At that time, Maitreya Buddha silently accepted the invitation and addressed the Brahma King, saying:

"Throughout the long night, I have endured great suffering while practicing the six perfections; only today has the ocean of Dharma been filled. I shall now raise the banner of Dharma, beat the drum of Dharma, blow the conch of Dharma, and rain down the rain of Dharma; I am about to preach the Dharma for you all."
The wheel of the Eightfold Noble Path turned by all Buddhas is one that no devas or humans can turn;
its meaning is impartial and leads directly to the unsurpassed, being unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and quiescent (*śānta*), serving to sever the suffering of sentient beings throughout the long night.

This Dharma is profoundly deep, difficult to attain and difficult to enter, difficult to believe and difficult to understand; there is none in all the world who can know it or see it, yet it washes away the defilements of the mind and brings about the attainment of the ten thousand pure practices (*brahmacarya*).

When these words were spoken, there were again countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of deva sons and daughters, as well as Great Brahma Kings from other directions, riding upon celestial palaces. They brought celestial flowers and incense to offer to the Tathāgata, circumambulated him a hundred thousand times, prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, and joined their palms in entreaty;
meanwhile, the various celestial musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck.
Then, the various Brahma Kings, with one voice and in unison, spoke these verses:
“For immeasurable and incalculable eons, Time has passed in vain without a Buddha;
Sentient beings have fallen into the evil realms, And the Eye of the World has been extinguished.”
The three evil realms have expanded and widened, and the paths to the heavens are forever severed;
today the Buddha has arisen in the world, and the three evil realms are utterly extinguished.
May he increase the hosts of devas and humans, and open the gate of the ambrosia of immortality.
Causing the minds of the multitude to be free from attachment, May they swiftly attain nirvana.
We Brahma Kings, Having heard that the Buddha has appeared in the world;
Now we have encountered the Buddha, The Unsurpassed Great Dharma King.
The Brahmā palace is magnificent, and his bodily radiance is likewise brilliant;
for the sake of the multitudes throughout the ten directions, he universally exhorts the Great Teacher:
"We pray only that you open the nectar-gate and turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma."
Having spoken these verses, he prostrated with his head at [the Buddha’s] feet and again joined his palms,
earnestly making this request three times: “I only pray, World-Honored One,

that you will turn the profound and subtle wheel of Dharma, to uproot the seeds of suffering and affliction for sentient beings, to bring them far away from the three poisons, and to destroy the unwholesome karma of the four evil realms.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, for the sake of the Brahma kings, immediately smiled and emitted five-colored rays of light, silently granting his permission.
Then the innumerable great assembly of devaputras, hearing the Buddha’s consent, were filled with immeasurable joy; their entire bodies leaped with exultation.
It was just as when a filial son who has recently suffered the loss of a parent sees his compassionate father suddenly return to life—the joy of the great assembly was likewise so.
Then the assembly of devas circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right for countless circuits; their reverence and affection were insatiable, and they withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the great multitude all thought to themselves:

"Though one were to enjoy the pleasures of the five desires for a thousand billion years, one cannot escape the suffering of the three evil realms; neither wife, children, nor wealth and property can provide salvation."
"The world is impermanent, and life is difficult to preserve for long; we should now, within the Buddha-dharma, purely cultivate the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
Having formed this thought, he further reflected:

"Even if one were to experience the five desires for countless eons—such as the immeasurable billions of years of lifespan in the Heaven of No-Thought, enjoying oneself with celestial maidens and receiving the touch of fine, smooth textures—all would ultimately end in destruction, leading to a fall into the three evil realms to undergo immeasurable suffering."

What one delights in is but slight, like a magical illusion and hardly worth mentioning; yet when entering hell, the great fires blaze forth, and for hundreds of millions of kalpas one undergoes immeasurable suffering—how could one hope to find liberation?
"Thus, throughout this long night, suffering and distress have been difficult to extricate; now that you have encountered the Buddha today, you should apply yourself with diligent vigor.
At that time, King Śakra raised his voice and proclaimed:
"Even if one is born into the bliss of the heavens, In the end, it too shall return to destruction."
"Before long we shall fall into hell, like a mass of fierce fire.
We ought to quickly leave the household life and study the Buddha-way.
Having spoken these words, King Śakra was then respectfully surrounded by eighty-four thousand ministers.

When the Four Heavenly Kings escorted the Wheel-Turning King to the Dragon-Flower Tree in the Flower Forest Garden, he went before Maitreya Buddha to seek ordination. Having paid homage to the Buddha, before his head had even been raised, his hair and beard fell away of their own accord, the saṃghāṭī robe appeared upon his body, and he immediately became a śramaṇa.

"At that time, Maitreya Buddha, together with King Śaṅkha, surrounded by eighty-four thousand ministers, various bhikṣus, and others, as well as countless devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings, entered the city of Ketumatī."

As his feet stepped upon the threshold of the gate, the Sahā world shook in six ways, and the land of Jambudvīpa turned the color of gold. In the center of the great city of Ketumatī, where the ground was adamantine, there was a precious adamantine throne upon which the Buddhas of the past had sat; this throne spontaneously emerged, surrounded by rows of trees made of various jewels.

In the sky, the devas rained down great jeweled flowers; the dragon kings performed various kinds of music and emitted flowers from their mouths—showering flowers from every pore—to make offerings to the Buddha.

At this seat, the Buddha turned the wheel of the true Dharma, declaring: "This is suffering—the Noble Truth of Suffering; this is its origin—the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering; this is its cessation—the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering; this is the path—the Noble Truth of the Path."
Furthermore, he expounded for them the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment that assist toward awakening, and also proclaimed the twelve links of dependent origination:

ignorance conditions volitional formations; volitional formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form; name-and-form conditions the six sense bases; the six sense bases condition contact; contact conditions sensation; sensation conditions craving; craving conditions clinging; clinging conditions becoming; becoming conditions birth; and birth conditions old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and distress.

"At that time, the great earth shook in six ways, and this sound was heard throughout the trichiliocosm, extending even further beyond measure and boundlessness, reaching downward as far as the Avīci Hell and upward as high as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven."
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings each led countless spirits and deities, crying out in a loud voice:

"When the Sun of the Buddha rises, it brings down the rain and dew of the Dharma; the Eye of the World is now first opened, so that all the eight classes of beings throughout the great earth who have a karmic affinity with the Buddha may all hear and know."

The gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven, and even up to the Mahābrahmā Heaven, each proclaimed in a loud voice within their respective domains:
"The Buddha-sun has appeared in the world and pours down the nectar of immortality! The Eye of the World is now opened; all those with whom he has a karmic affinity shall hear and know this."

At that time, the various dragon kings and the eight classes of beings—the mountain deities, tree deities, medicinal herb deities, water deities, wind deities, fire deities, earth deities, city and moat deities, and household deities—leaped for joy and shouted aloud:

Furthermore, there were eighty-four thousand brahmins, all of whom were intelligent and possessed great wisdom; they also followed the Great King to leave the household life and study the Way within the Buddha-dharma.
Furthermore, there was an elder named Sudatta—who is the present Elder Sudatta—and he also went forth from home together with eighty-four thousand people.
There were also the brothers Liśāda and Pūraṇa, who likewise went forth from home together with eighty-four thousand people.

Furthermore, there were two chief ministers—one named Brahmamallī and the other named Sumana—who were dearly cherished by the king; they also, together with eighty-four thousand people, left the household life to study the Way within the Buddha-dharma.
The wheel-turning king’s precious daughter was named Śyāmavatī; she is the present mother of Viśākhā, and she too renounced the world together with eighty-four thousand court ladies.
The crown prince of Śakra was named Suvarṇavarṇa; he is now the son of the elder Trapuṣa, and he has likewise gone forth from the household life together with eighty-four thousand people.

The son of a brahmin from Maitreya Buddha’s own clan, named Sumati, who possessed sharp faculties and wisdom, is now the son of the bhikṣuṇī Uttara-Subhadra; he too, together with sixty thousand others, has gone forth as a renunciant within the Buddha-dharma.

Of King Śaṅkha’s thousand sons, he retained only one to succeed him on the throne; the remaining nine hundred and ninety-nine sons, together with eighty-four thousand others, all went forth as monastics within the Buddha-dharma.
Thus, these immeasurable billions of beings, seeing the world’s suffering and the blazing of the five aggregates, all together renounced the householder’s life within the Dharma of Maitreya Buddha.
At that time, Maitreya Buddha, with a heart of great compassion, addressed the great assembly, saying:

"You have now come to me neither for the sake of the joy of rebirth in heaven, nor for the sake of the pleasures of this present life; you have come solely for the causes and conditions of the eternal bliss of Nirvana. All these people have planted various roots of goodness within the Buddha-dharma."

Śākyamuni Buddha appeared in this world of five turbidities and, through various reproaches, preached the Dharma for your sake; yet there was nothing he could do for you, so he taught you to plant the seeds of future conditions.

Now that you have been able to see me, I shall now accept these people: those who, by reciting, analyzing, and definitively determining the Sūtras, Vinaya, and Abhidharma, expound them for others, praise their meaning and flavor, refrain from jealousy, and teach others so that they may uphold them, thereby cultivating various merits to be born in my presence;
or those who give clothing and food to others, observe the precepts, and possess wisdom, cultivating such merits to be born in my presence.
Some have made offerings to the Buddha with music, banners, canopies, flowers, incense, and lamps; having cultivated such merit, they have been reborn in my presence.

Some have provided the Sangha with constant food, established monastic dwellings, and offered the four requisites; by observing the eightfold precepts and practicing loving-kindness, they have cultivated such merit and been reborn in my presence.

Others, out of deep compassion for suffering beings, have taken their place to undergo their pain and enabled them to find happiness; having cultivated such merit, they have been reborn in my presence.
Some, by means of upholding the precepts and practicing patience, cultivate a pure mind of loving-kindness; through these merits, they come to be born in my presence.

Others construct monasteries for the four quarters without obstruction, establish assemblies for fasting and lectures, and provide offerings of food and drink; through the cultivation of such merits, they come to be born in my presence.

Still others, by means of upholding the precepts, extensive learning, and the practice of meditative concentration and untainted wisdom (*anāsrava-prajñā*), through these merits, come to be born in my presence.
Some may erect stupas to make offerings to the *śarīra*, or contemplate the *dharmakāya* of the Buddha; by virtue of these merits, they come to be born in my presence.

Some may be beset by calamity and distress, poverty, or solitude; bound to others, or subject to royal law, facing execution, or having performed karma leading to the eight difficulties (*aṣṭākṣaṇa*), they undergo great suffering and affliction—I rescue them and cause them to attain liberation, and by cultivating these merits, they come to be born in my presence.

Some may suffer the pain of separation from loved ones, or the extreme anguish of factionalism and litigation—I employ skillful means to bring about their reconciliation, and by cultivating these merits, they come to be born in my presence.
Having spoken these words, he praised Śākyamuni Buddha, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!

You are able, in this world of five turbidities, to teach and transform hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of such evil sentient beings, causing them to cultivate the roots of goodness so that they may come to be born in my presence."
At that time, Maitreya Buddha praised Śākyamuni Buddha in this way three times,
and spoke these verses: “The patient, courageous, and great Teacher, Who, within this unwholesome world of the five turbidities,
Transforms and brings to maturity evil sentient beings, Causing them to practice and attain the vision of a Buddha.”
Having borne the burden of sentient beings and undergone great suffering, you have now entered the state of eternal bliss and non-action;
I instruct those disciples to come to my place.
I shall now expound the Four Noble Truths for you, as well as the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the twelve links of dependent origination that adorn nirvana.
"You all should observe the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and enter into the state of emptiness and stillness, the place where there is originally nothing.
Having spoken this verse, he further praised them, saying:
"In that time of suffering and evil, those sentient beings were able to perform what is difficult to do."
Among those possessed of greed, hatred, delusion, confusion, and short lifespans, to be able to cultivate and maintain the precepts and perform various meritorious deeds is truly most rare.
At that time, sentient beings did not recognize their parents, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas; they did not know the way of the Dharma and instead harmed one another, drawing near to the kalpa of weapons.

Deeply attached to the five desires, they were envious, sycophantic, crooked, turbid, perverse, and deceitful; lacking any heart of compassion, they slaughtered and harmed one another, eating flesh and drinking blood.
They did not respect their teachers or elders, did not recognize virtuous friends, and did not know how to repay kindness.
Born into an age of the five turbidities, they lack a sense of shame and remorse;

day and night, throughout the six periods, they continuously commit evil without knowing contentment, creating nothing but unwholesome deeds and a mass of the five heinous crimes, all piled together like fish scales.
They seek [sensual gratification] without ever tiring of it, and their nine types of kinsmen and clans cannot provide mutual aid.
Excellent, excellent!
Śākyamuni Buddha!

By means of great skillful means and profound compassion, you are able, amidst suffering and distressed sentient beings, with a serene countenance and beautiful appearance, through skillful wisdom, to speak words of truth and show me that you shall come in the future to deliver and liberate us all.

Thus, this Guide possesses sharp and penetrating wisdom, rare in the world and extremely difficult to encounter; with a profound heart of compassion for the sentient beings of this degenerate age, he acts to uproot their suffering and distress, enabling them to attain peace and security and enter the ultimate, profoundly deep nature of phenomena.

For three asaṃkhyeya kalpas, Śākyamuni, for your sake, practiced difficult and painful austerities; he gave away his head as alms and cut off his ears, nose, hands, feet, and limbs, undergoing all manner of suffering and affliction for the sake of the Eightfold Noble Path and equal liberation, in order to benefit you.
"At that time, Maitreya Buddha will thus instruct and guide immeasurable sentient beings, causing them to rejoice.

At that time, the bodies of those beings will be purely Dharma, their minds will be purely Dharma, and their mouths will constantly preach the Dharma. Persons of merit and wisdom will fill the realm, and devas and humans will revere, believe, accept, and yearn for it with longing."
At that time, the Great Guide, wishing each of them to hear of their past sufferings and afflictions, further thought to himself:
"The five desires are impure; they are the root of all suffering."
Furthermore, he is able to eliminate and abandon sorrow, grief, and resentment, and understands that the phenomena of suffering and pleasure are all impermanent; for their sake, he teaches:
"Form, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are suffering, empty, impermanent, and non-self."

When these words were spoken, nine hundred and sixty million people did not grasp at any phenomena; their outflows were exhausted, their minds were liberated, and they attained arhatship, possessing the three insights, the six supernormal powers, and the eight liberations.
Three hundred and sixty thousand devaputras and two hundred thousand devakanyās resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Among the eight classes of supernatural beings, including devas and nāgas, there were those who attained the stage of *srotāpanna*, those who planted the causal conditions for the path of a *pratyekabuddha*, and those who resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed path; their number was so vast as to be beyond calculation.

"At that time, Maitreya Buddha, surrounded by a great assembly of nine hundred and sixty million bhikṣus, as well as King Śaṅkha and eighty-four thousand ministers and their retinues of bhikṣus, like the Moon Deity followed by the various constellations, departed from the city of Ketumatī and returned to the multi-storied lecture hall in the Flower Forest Garden."
At that time, the cities, towns, and villages of Jambudvīpa—the minor kings, elders, and those of the four castes—all gathered beneath the Dragon Flower tree in the Flower Forest Garden.
"At that time, the World-Honored One again preached the Four Noble Truths and the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination; ninety-four billion people attained arhatship.

Furthermore, gods from other directions and the eight classes of beings—sixty-four billion as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—gave rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and dwelt in the stage of non-retrogression."
"In the third great assembly, nine hundred and twenty billion people attained arhatship;
three hundred and forty billion devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

"At that time, after Maitreya Buddha had turned the profound and wondrous Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths and delivered gods and humans, he led his assembly of śrāvaka disciples, the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and so forth, into the city to beg for food. Immeasurable hosts of Śuddhāvāsa devas followed the Buddha with reverence as they entered the city of Ketumatī."

Upon entering the city, the Buddha manifested eighteen kinds of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*): from his lower body water issued forth like *maṇi* jewels, transforming into a radiant platform that illuminated the worlds of the ten directions;
from his upper body fire issued forth like Mount Sumeru, streaming with purple-gold light;
he appeared filling the great void, transforming it into lapis lazuli.
The large again manifests as small, like a mustard seed, until it vanishes without a trace;
it leaps up in the ten directions and sinks down in the ten directions, causing all people to become like the body of a Buddha.
Through various supernormal powers and immeasurable transformations, he caused all those with the karmic affinity to attain liberation.

Śakra Devānām-Indra, together with his thirty-two ministers and the devas of the desire realm, and Brahmā Rāja, together with the devas of the form realm, along with their sons and daughters, removed their celestial necklaces and heavenly garments and scattered them over the Buddha; at that time, the heavenly garments transformed into flower canopies.
The celestial music played spontaneously without being struck, as they sang praises of the Buddha’s virtues.
A fine rain of celestial flowers and a blend of sandalwood incenses were offered to the Buddha;
banners and streamers were erected along the streets, lanes, and pathways, and various famous incenses were burned, their smoke rising like clouds.
When the World-Honored One entered the city, Mahābrahmā and Śakra-devendra joined their palms in reverent salutation and praised the Buddha with these verses:
“The Perfectly All-Knowing One, the Honored One among two-legged beings, In the world of devas and humans, there is none equal to you.
The World-Honored One of Ten Powers is most rare and marvelous; He is the unsurpassed, supreme, and excellent field of merit.”
Those who make offerings to him are born in the heavens; in the future, they will attain liberation and abide in nirvana.
I bow my head to the Unsurpassed One of Great Diligence; I bow my head to the Compassionate Great Teacher.

“The Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the East, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka of the South, the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa of the West, and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa of the North, together with their retinues, joined their palms in reverence and,
with pure minds, praised the World-Honored One: “‘Peerless throughout the three realms, Adorned by great compassion yourself,
You have realized the ultimate truth.’”
Together with all dharmas and their characteristics, they enter equally into the nature of emptiness and stillness,
abiding well in non-existence.
Although they practice great diligence, they are unconditioned and leave no trace.
I now prostrate in homage to the Great Guide of Compassionate Heart.
For a long night I have undergone birth and death, falling into the three evil realms and taking on the body of a woman.
Today the Buddha has arisen in the world, uprooting suffering and bestowing peace and happiness; the three evil realms have already diminished.
May women, free from deceit and crookedness, all attain cessation.
Fully endowed with Great Nirvāṇa, the one who delivers beings from suffering through great compassion appears in the world to bestow happiness.
Constantly bestowing all forms of joy, he neither kills nor harms others.
With a mind of forbearance like the great earth,
I now prostrate and pay homage to the Great Teacher of Patience;
I now prostrate and pay homage to the Great Being of Compassion.
"Having liberated myself from the suffering of birth and death, I am able to uproot the calamities of sentient beings;
like a lotus blooming within fire, there is nothing in the world that can compare.

At that time, the World-Honored One went on his alms-round in succession, returned with the bhikṣus to his original location, and entered deep meditative concentration, remaining silent and unmoving for seven days and seven nights.

The disciples of Maitreya Buddha will have complexions like those of the gods; they will all be upright and handsome. Disgusted with birth, old age, sickness, and death, they will be widely learned and deeply studied, guarding the treasury of the Dharma and practicing meditative concentration. Having attained liberation from all desires, they will be like birds emerging from their shells.
At that time, Śakra Devānām-indra, together with the sons of the gods of the desire realm, rejoiced and leaped for joy, and further spoke in verse:
“The Great Teacher to whom the world turns, Whose eye of wisdom is clear and pure, seeing the ten directions;
Whose power of knowledge and merit surpass those of all devas, Endowed with both name and meaning, he brings blessings to sentient beings.”
We pray that for the sake of us, the multitude of sentient beings, you will lead your disciples to that mountain;
there we shall make offerings to the Teacher Śākyamuni, who is free from affliction, and to his foremost great disciple of dhūta practices.
We should be able to behold the Buddha in person, Don his saffron robes, and hear his bequeathed Dharma;
Repenting the turbid and evil kalpas of our former lives, May our unwholesome and evil karmas be purified.
“At that time, Maitreya Buddha, together with the former beings of the Sahā world who had been stubborn and difficult to transform, as well as his great disciples, all went to Vulture Peak Mountain.”
Having reached the foot of the mountain, he proceeded with calm and slow steps up Mount Wolf’s Track (Vṛka-pada).
Upon reaching the summit, he lifted his big toe and pressed it against the mountain base; at that moment, the great earth shook in eighteen ways.
Having reached the summit of the mountain, Maitreya split the mountain apart with his hands toward both sides, like a Wheel-Turning King opening the great gates of a city.
At that time, the Brahma King took celestial fragrant oil and poured it over Mahākāśyapa’s head; once the oil had drenched his body, he struck the great gong and blew the great conch shell.

Mahākāśyapa immediately arose from the meditative absorption of cessation, adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and taking the saṃghāṭī robe of Śākyamuni Buddha, presented it to Maitreya, saying:
"The Great Master Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, at the time of his parinirvāṇa, entrusted this Dharma robe to me, commanding me to offer it to the World-Honored One."
Then, the great assembly each addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How is it that today on this mountain peak there is a 'human-head worm,' short and ugly, wearing the robes of a śramaṇa, who is able to pay homage and show reverence to the World-Honored One?"
At that time, Maitreya Buddha rebuked his great disciples, telling them not to despise this person, and spoke these verses:
“The peacock has beautiful colors, yet it is devoured by hawks, falcons, and hawks;
The white elephant possesses immeasurable strength, yet the cub of a lion, though small, [overcomes it].”
They seize food like grains of dust;
though the great dragon’s body is immeasurable, it is struck down by the garuḍa;
though a human body may be tall and large, plump, white, and handsome;
A jar of the seven precious gems filled with excrement is so foul and filthy as to be unbearable.
Although this person is short and small in stature, his wisdom is like refined gold;
having long since exhausted the habitual tendencies of affliction, he is free from the remainder of the suffering of birth and death, and dwells here for the sake of protecting the Dharma.
Constantly practicing the dhūta austerities, he is the most excellent among gods and humans;
his asceticism is peerless.
He has been sent to my presence; you all should be single-minded.
"Joining their palms in reverent salutation.
Having spoken this verse, he addressed the bhikṣus:

"Among the one thousand two hundred and fifty disciples of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni, who teaches sentient beings in this world of five turbidities, there is one foremost in dhūta practices, whose body is golden in color. He abandoned his golden-skinned wife to leave the home life and study the Way; day and night he was diligent as if his head were on fire, and out of compassion for poor, suffering, and lowly beings, he constantly brought them across through blessings. This Mahākāśyapa, who remains in the world for the sake of the Dharma, is this very person."
Having spoken these words, the entire great assembly prostrated themselves in homage.

At that time, Maitreya took up the saṃghāṭī robe of Śākyamuni Buddha; he covered his right hand with it, but it did not reach beyond barely masking two fingers, and he likewise covered his left hand, which also masked only two fingers.
All the people marveled and sighed in wonder:
"The previous Buddhas were humble and lowly; this was entirely due to the greed, turbidity, and arrogance of sentient beings.
He then addressed Mahākāśyapa, saying:
"You may now manifest your supernatural powers and proclaim all the sūtras and teachings of the past Buddhas."
At that time, Mahākāśyapa leaped into the air and performed the eighteen transformations: he manifested a massive body that filled the void of space;
from that great form he again manifested a small one like a mustard seed, and from that small form he again manifested a great one;
water issued from the upper part of his body, while fire issued from the lower part of his body.
He walked on the earth as if on water, and walked on water as if on earth; he sat and lay down in mid-air without his body sinking or falling.

He leaped up in the east and sank in the west, leaped up in the west and sank in the east, leaped up in the south and sank in the north, leaped up in the north and sank in the south, leaped up at the edge and sank in the center, leaped up in the center and sank at the edge, leaped up above and sank below, and leaped up below and sank above.
Within the void of space, he manifested a grotto made of lapis lazuli.
Empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, he spoke the twelve divisions of the *sūtras* of Śākyamuni Buddha with a Brahma-like voice.
Having heard this, the great assembly marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
Eight billion people were distanced from dust and freed from defilement; regarding all phenomena, they did not grasp at any phenomena and attained arhatship.

Innumerable devas and humans gave rise to the bodhicitta, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and descended from the air to pay homage to the Buddha, declaring that all conditioned phenomena are entirely impermanent.
Taking his leave of the Buddha, he retired and returned to Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain, his original dwelling place;
from his body he emitted fire and entered parinirvāṇa.
His bodily relics were collected, and a stupa was erected upon the mountain peak.
Maitreya Buddha praised him, saying:

"The bhikṣu Mahākāśyapa was constantly extolled by Śākyamuni Buddha among the great assembly as the foremost in dhūta practices. He has attained mastery in dhyāna, samādhi, and liberation. Although he possesses great supernormal powers, he is free from arrogance; he is able to bring great joy to sentient beings and always takes pity on those who are lowly, poor, and suffering."
Maitreya Buddha praised the skeletal remains of Mahākāśyapa, saying:
"Excellent, O one of great spiritual power!
"O Mahākāśyapa, great disciple of the Lion of the Śākyas!
You were able to cultivate your mind in that evil age.
At that time, the skeletal remains of Mahākāśyapa spoke these verses:
“The dhūta practices are a treasure-trove; upholding the precepts is nectar.
Those who can practice the dhūtas will surely reach the deathless ground.”
"By upholding the precepts, one attains birth in the heavens, as well as the bliss of nirvāṇa.
Having spoken this verse, it returned into the stūpa like water of lapis lazuli.
“At that time, the place where the Dharma was being taught was eighty yojanas wide and one hundred yojanas long;
among the multitude of people there, whether sitting or standing, near or far, each saw the Buddha before them alone, preaching the Dharma to them.”
“Maitreya Buddha shall remain in the world for sixty trillion years; out of compassion for sentient beings, he will cause them to attain the Dharma-eye.

After his parinirvāṇa, the devas and people of the world shall cremate the Buddha’s body, and at that time a Wheel-Turning King shall collect the relics and erect eighty-four thousand stupas throughout the four continents.
The True Dharma shall remain in the world for sixty thousand years, and the Semblance Dharma for twenty thousand years.”

"You all should apply yourselves with diligent vigor, give rise to a pure mind, and cultivate various wholesome deeds; then you will undoubtedly behold the body of Maitreya Buddha, the Lamp of Illumination for the World."
When the Buddha had finished speaking, the Venerable Śāriputra and the Venerable Ānanda rose from their seats, prostrated before the Buddha, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"What should this sutra be named?
How should it be upheld?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Remember this well and expound it in detail for the sake of gods and humans; do not become one who severs the Dharma at its end.

This essential teaching is called ‘The Severing of the Roots of the Five Heinous Crimes by All Sentient Beings,’ which purifies karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions, and afflictive obstructions, and involves cultivating a mind of loving-kindness to practice together with Maitreya—thus you should uphold it.
It is also called ‘The Sutra on All Sentient Beings Hearing the Name of Maitreya Buddha and Certainly Escaping the Five Turbidities and Not Falling into Evil Realms’—thus you should uphold it.”
It is also called the *Sūtra on Breaking Evil Verbal Karma and the Mind Like a Lotus, Clearly Seeing Maitreya Buddha*; one should uphold it thus.
It is also called the *Sūtra on Compassionate Mind, Non-killing, and Not Eating Meat*; one should uphold it thus.
It is also called the *Sūtra on Śākyamuni Buddha Using His Robe as a Token of Faith*; one should uphold it thus.
It is also titled *The Sutra on How Hearing the Buddha’s Name Ensures One Will Certainly Escape the Eight Difficulties*, and should be upheld as such;
it is also titled *The Sutra on Maitreya’s Attainment of Buddhahood*, and should be upheld as such.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and the eight classes of beings—gods, nāgas, and other spirits—hear this sūtra, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, pay homage to it, make offerings to it, and revere the Dharma masters, they shall destroy all karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions, and afflictive obstructions. They shall behold Maitreya and the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa; the three types of bodhi shall be accomplished according to their vows; they shall not take on female bodies; they shall leave the household life with right view and attain great liberation.”
When these words had been spoken, the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all filled with great joy; they prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
*The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Great Attainment of Buddhahood*.
